A part of a city represented by a council member.
Cleveland’s 2026 council has 15 wards. Wards are inside Cleveland, not separate cities.
The place or kind of problem a public body has legal power to handle.
A city office cannot decide every state utility question.
A law made by a city or other local government.
Cleveland uses ordinances for local housing and parking rules.
A proposal for a law that has not necessarily become law.
The Ohio General Assembly considers state bills.
A local voting area used to organize elections.
Check the county election office for the precinct tied to your address.
The official list of candidates and questions you can vote on.
Your address and the election determine your ballot.
A tax measure used to raise money for a public purpose.
A school levy may raise operating money; read its exact ballot language.
Borrowed money that must be repaid, usually with interest.
A bond may help pay for school buildings over time.
A part of government responsible for a group of services.
Building and Housing handles inspections and code enforcement.
The local document that organizes a city’s government and powers.
Cleveland’s charter defines municipal offices and duties.
Permission in a budget to spend public money for a stated purpose.
Permission to spend is not proof that a payment has happened.
An official who formally introduces or supports a proposal in the legislative process.
Being listed as a sponsor is different from a recorded yes vote.
A smaller group that reviews a subject before the full public body acts.
A council committee can hold hearings and recommend action.
A request for another court or authorized body to review a decision.
The correct appeal path depends on the case and applicable law.
The official list of filings and events in a case.
A docket helps you find case documents and hearing entries.
The official who hears a court case and makes legal decisions.
A judge’s role is different from a mayor’s or council member’s.
An organization providing a service such as electricity or water.
Cleveland Public Power is a city-owned electric utility.
A contract to buy electricity under stated terms.
A utility can buy power without owning the plant.
Instructions about which available power resources produce electricity for grid needs.
Grid operation is separate from plant ownership.
The price or pricing rules used to charge for a service.
Your electric bill can include different kinds of charges.
The public body responsible for governing a school district.
CMSD has a mayor-appointed board; not all districts use that system.
A boundary used for a particular service, election, or public body.
A school district and a council ward can have different boundaries.
Local rules about how land and buildings may be used.
Zoning can shape where homes, stores, or factories can be built.
Official permission for a specific activity, subject to rules.
A building project may need a city permit.
Checking how an organization uses its powers and follows rules.
Oversight does not always mean direct control of daily work.
An agreement setting out the parties’ duties and terms.
A public contract should identify price, duration, and approval records.
The process a public body uses to buy goods or services.
A purchasing process can lead to a contract with a vendor.
A legal power to make a particular decision.
Funding an organization is not the same as controlling all its decisions.
The date a rule begins to apply.
An ordinance’s passage date may be earlier than its effective date.
A formal change to a proposal, law, or agreement.
Read a contract’s amendments along with the original agreement.
